title: In many ways (Hebrews 1:1–4)
hookLine: God spoke through prophets in many ways, and now by a Son
tomorrow: was Jesus ever really tempted, in a body like ours?

lines: GOD TOLD ME TO TAKE THE JOB.
cards: Somebody at a dinner table says, God told me to take the job. Half the table nods. The other half goes quiet.

Then a cousin mentions a dream that wouldn't let go of her for a week. Does God still speak like that, or has God already said it all? Christians disagree about it, and both sides open to the same page.
A new book today, Hebrews, a letter that never names its writer. And its very first sentence is about God speaking.

teach.b: Here it is: "God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son." Sundry times, divers manners: bit by bit, in many ways.
Now, a Son, "the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person." Then one plain act: he purged our sins, and "sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high."
Sat down, the way someone does when the work is finished. So which way does all that point? Two views, both inside the faith.

teach.h: AN OPEN DOOR: OLD MEN SHALL DREAM.
teach.b: Some Christians, Pentecostal and charismatic believers for example, hear an open door. The God who spoke in many ways still does: a dream, a nudge, a word through a friend.
They point to Acts, where Peter quotes the prophet Joel: "your old men shall dream dreams."
Other Christians, some in Reformed churches for example, hear a final word.
God has spoken in the Son, fully, and the scriptures carry that word; a claimed new message can mislead. They point to the verb itself: hath spoken.

Both sides can reach for one test from Paul: "Despise not prophesyings. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good." And both agree on where the sentence lands: in Jesus, they say, the speaking has a face.

how: Hebrews 1:1–4 is read in some churches at Christmas. Christians differ on whether God still speaks through dreams and prophecy today, and some test what they hear against scripture.

games.q: you lean toward 'God still speaks in dreams and nudges.' your friend leans toward 'God has spoken fully in the Son.' what's the best case for her side?
o: Hebrews says hath spoken: claimed new messages can mislead, so scripture is the measure.
she thinks God never cared to speak to anyone at all.
she just doesn't like dreams; it's a matter of taste.
games.why: her side reads the same verse as a final word, spoken in the Son. yours hears many ways, and Joel's dreams in Acts. both can hold Paul's test: prove all things.

practice: Listen for a single sound where you are, a fan, a bird, a car, your own breath, and stay with just that one. When another sound or thought cuts in, let it pass and come back to the first.
If listening for God is part of your life, this can be that kind of listening too.

wordCard.voice: In many ways. The first words of Hebrews: God spoke to the fathers by the prophets in many ways, and now by a Son.

orig.note: Greek: in many ways; one of two sound-alike words that open Hebrews 1:1.

carryVoice: Keep this: God has spoken, a tense Christians read two ways, and both start there. Until tomorrow.
